articles.title: Matt LaFleur shredded by Packers fans after team collapses vs Vikings
articles.summary: Matt LaFleur's decision to take points off the board in fourth quarter of eventual loss to Vikings is leaving Packers fans frustrated.
articles.body:
It's a new season for the Green Bay Packers but you couldn't tell based on what happened at U.S. Bank Stadium.

Matt LaFleur's Packers picked up right where they left off in blowing leads.

The Packers held a double-digit third-quarter lead, 22-10, against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Sept. 13, as they controlled the game from the beginning. You wouldn't know by looking at the final score.

The Packers not only lost, but were blown out in a disastrous finish, losing 39-22, as the Vikings scored the game's final 29 points.

Packers fans saw all of this last year, most notably in the team's wild-card epic collapse against the Chicago Bears when they allowed 25 fourth-quarter points. The Vikings outscored the Packers, 22-0, in this fourth quarter.

While it was a combination of events again that led to this meltdown, a decision that LaFleur made to take points off the board with the Packers ahead 22-17 early in the fourth quarter set the stage for this new collapse.

Trey Smack made a field goal to put the Packers ahead 25-17 but LaFleur decided to take 5 yards after a Vikings penalty instead of taking the three points. The Packers then faced a 4th and 1. He called a quarterback sneak and Love was stopped.

The Vikings went down and scored on the next possession. The momentum had changed and soon Collapse No. 1 in 2026 was complete.

Packers fans sound off on Matt LaFleur after loss to Vikings

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: “It’s on us” after 12 penalties in loss to Minnesota Vikings
articles.summary: Twelve flags for 98 yards. Five of them gave the Minnesota Vikings a first down. The Green Bay Packers were penalized four times as often as Minnesota at U.S...
articles.body:
Twelve flags for 98 yards. Five of them gave the Minnesota Vikings a first down. The Green Bay Packers were penalized four times as often as Minnesota at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday.

Minnesota was flagged three times for 15 yards in a 39-22 win.

Green Bay led 22-10 in the third quarter and outgained the Vikings 419-239 for the game.

Matt LaFleur told the team not to put it in the officials' hands

LaFleur got a question about three straight third-down penalties on one Minnesota drive.

"Yeah, it is," he said. "I mean, obviously, it had an effect because they were able to go down the score, and then we get the pick in the end zone. We get called for, was it DPI or holding? I don't know. I thought a lot of times that, like, you know, those plays happened down there, but they called it. So my point to the team is you can't put it in the hands of the officials."

Earlier in the same availability he had already gotten there: "Far too many penalties tonight."

Tucker Kraft and Christian Watson landed in the same place

Kraft, a captain for the first time Sunday, put the fourth quarter on Green Bay and nowhere else.

"Yeah, it's just a combination of mental errors and penalties," the tight end said. "I mean, in penalties, we're in control of our own actions. It's just we've got to clean that up. That's the only way we're going to grow as a program and be able to beat good teams."

Christian Watson, who scored both Packers touchdowns, was asked how much the penalties mattered.

"I mean, it was huge," Watson said. "I mean, we can't put stuff like that in the ref's hands. We've got to find a way to be disciplined and play sound football and avoid getting those things because I mean as much as you know anyone would want to argue each you know either way you know we put it in their hands I mean it's on us."

Safety Evan Williams framed it as a September problem that does not have to stay one.

"You see it a lot more early in the season," Williams said. "You know, just you see the impact of, you know, playing discipline versus not playing discipline and how that can change a game, you know, flip a game on its head."

Williams kept going, into the part that showed up in the fourth quarter.

"It's just, you know, doing the little things right, you know, just having the mental fortitude late in the game when you're tired, when it's late in drives to find a way to get off the field and do exactly what you're supposed to do," he said. "I feel like we put ourselves in a good spot, but at the end of the day, I said it before, but can't leave it up to the refs to make those type of calls. Just move forward. That's all you can do."

Matt LaFleur says the negative plays opened the floodgates

"When we got behind the sticks, if we had a negative play, a negative run, it just opens up the floodgates, and then it's a guessing game," LaFleur said. "Are they bringing it? Are they bluffing you? But that's the game they want to play."

Kraft said the same thing from the huddle's side of it. "And when we're constantly behind the sticks like that, that's where that defense thrives," he said. "And they took it to us."

Minnesota scored 22 points in the fourth quarter, three touchdowns inside a span of 2 minutes and 39 seconds. Green Bay was stopped twice on fourth down, lost a fumble and threw an interception.

Green Bay plays at the New York Jets on Sunday at noon CT.

articles.title: Frederick Country Club host 7th Annual Charity Golf Scramble
articles.summary: The Frederick County Club will be holding a special tournament next month. The 7th Annual Golf Scramble will be taking place on Friday, Oct. 16, at 9 a.m., w...
articles.body:
FREDERICK ( KFDX/KJTL ) — The Frederick County Club is hosting a special tournament next month. The 7th Annual Golf Scramble will take place on Friday, Oct. 16, at 9 a.m., with sign-in starting at 8:30 a.m., at the country club at 1001 N. 1st Street .

Each participant will play two rounds of nine holes, with a free lunch provided after the first round is completed.

This event is $50 per player or $200 for a group of four. It is free for all high school and college players.

This event will support Operation C.A.R.E and all proceeds will be used to fund the services provided by the nonprofit Operation C.A.R.E. Ministries of Tillman County to residents who are in need of assistance.

For more information about this event, contact Jay McPherson at (580) 305- 3346.

articles.title: North Texas annihilates UNLV, 44-6, for Neal Brown’s first win
articles.summary: North Texas’ retooled roster decisively outplays a Mountain West contender in every phase.
articles.body:
In September 2025, the Washington State social media team tweeted a preview graphic for its upcoming game against North Texas . The graphic depicted a desert, an oil rig, saguaro cacti, and an eagle in a cowboy hat with a holster. The depiction of Denton could not be more detached from reality, but North Texas' fanbase decided to embrace the misrepresentation, and the eagle from the graphic — 'Desert Scrappy' — became a program icon, embroidered on Neal Brown's polo at his weekly press conference.

North Texas beat Washington State, 59-10.

One year later, the UNLV social media team tweeted a hype video set to Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" for its looming game against North Texas, also depicting Denton as a desert atmosphere.

Any time another program is unsure what Denton looks like, North Texas takes them sightseeing. And the No. 1 attraction the Mean Green show on this sightseeing tour is the lopsided scoreboard at DATCU Stadium.

The Mean Green obliterated UNLV by 38 points to record the first win of Neal Brown's coaching tenure. It was a thorough domination from start to finish and the Rebels were held out of the end zone for the first time since Sept. 18, 2021. Meanwhile, under the direction of new defensive coordinator Matt Powledge, North Texas prevented an FBS opponent from scoring a touchdown for the first time since Sept. 21, 2019.

Hours earlier on Saturday, roughly 230 miles north, a significant portion of North Texas' 2025 roster and coaching staff — now at Oklahoma State — upset No. 6 Oregon . That result showcased the sheer amount of talent the Mean Green lost from 2025 to 2026. But Saturday afternoon in Denton proved how well the program reloaded under Coach Brown. North Texas handled the preseason Mountain West favorite in every phase of the game.

Offensively, quarterback Tayven Jackson spread the wealth around in a performance featuring 233 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown. Running back Jahiem White , who starred under Brown at West Virginia , looked fresh in his second game back from a knee injury, generating 124 rushing yards and a touchdown. With the former Big 12 starters leading the way, North Texas accrued 444 yards of offense against a UNLV defense which didn't allow more than 27 points in its first two contests.

Defensively, the Mean Green dominated the turnover battle, 4-0. North Texas, which accumulated the fifth-most takeaways in the FBS last season, continued the trend with a completely new staff and roster. Bryce Garza secured the lone interception of the game, while three different Mean Green players scooped up a fumble. The turnover creation was assisted by an assertive defensive line which registered four sacks against the Rebels, including 1.5 courtesy of UMass transfer defensive end David Onuoha.

Even on special teams, North Texas showed nothing but excellence in the Denton Desert. Kicker Dominic De Freitas sunk all three of his field goal attempts, producing the first six points of the game before North Texas fully settled in. From there, it was a steady beatdown, as North Texas unquestionably controlled the line of scrimmage on both sides.

UNLV (1-2, 1-0 Mountain West) is now 0-2 against the American Conference this season. The Rebels watched their Week 0 game against Memphis slip away in the second half, and this time, they weren't even in the same territory as their opponent. The inability to move the ball in the second half continues to plague UNLV, which has only scored 17 second half points in three games. These offensive struggles can be primarily attributed to the frontlines, as the Rebels were out-sacked by opponents, 10-2, in their two losses.

North Texas (1-1, 0-0 American) earned its first victory with Coach Brown and his significantly overturned roster. One week after playing respectably for a half against defending champion Indiana , North Texas found its full gear and obliterated what is expected to be one of the top teams in the Mountain West. The Mean Green now must return to the road and make a similar statement against a new Pac-12 team in Texas State.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: Edgerrin Cooper has run out of patience with the finishing talk
articles.summary: Edgerrin Cooper gave reporters five sentences on Sunday and one of them was about being finished with the subject. The Green Bay Packers defense held Minneso...
articles.body:
Edgerrin Cooper gave reporters five sentences on Sunday and one of them was about being finished with the subject. The Green Bay Packers defense held Minnesota to 239 total yards, knocked Kyler Murray out of the game in the first quarter and intercepted his first pass. It then gave up 22 points in the fourth quarter of a 39-22 loss at U.S. Bank Stadium.

Cooper did not want to do the postgame version of this again.

Edgerrin Cooper: 'I don't want to talk about it no more'

"No, just correct the things we need to correct," Cooper said. "We didn't finish. I'm tired of saying this every time. I don't want to talk about it no more, but it's what we got to do. So we just got to figure it out."

Green Bay ran 21 times for 66 yards and did not score after the third quarter.

"I don't think it's a question of the guys we have in the room," right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele said. "I think it's more so, can we execute and make plays when you need them?"

The defense played well enough for most of three quarters

Minnesota ran 61 plays for 239 yards and averaged 3.9 per snap. The Vikings threw for 151 yards as a team. Green Bay got three sacks and an interception and forced Minnesota into a 38-yard field goal on its only first-half scoring drive that did not end in the end zone.

LaFleur said the flags, not the coverage, extended the drives that mattered.

"Yeah, I thought our defense played really well," he said. "You know, again, there were some unfortunate penalties we had that extended drives, and then I thought in the fourth quarter especially, offensively we put them in some really tough positions."

Green Bay was flagged 12 times for 98 yards. Five of those penalties gave Minnesota a first down. The Vikings were flagged three times all afternoon.

Carson Wentz replaced the concussed Murray in the first quarter and threw three touchdown passes, two of them to Justin Jefferson . T.J. Hockenson caught the other. Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason ran for scores in the fourth, and Minnesota converted a two-point pass to Jefferson to take the lead for good.

The pass rush is still waiting on Micah Parsons

Green Bay played without Micah Parsons, who is on the reserve/physically unable to perform list while he recovers from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season and is ineligible to return before Week 5. Lukas Van Ness and the rest of the front got six quarterback hits.

CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson said during Sunday's broadcast that she asked Parsons whether he has Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys circled. He left the date open and told her, "We will see," per Dallas Sports Journal.

Franklin's read on the opener was more forward-looking than Cooper's.

"We're not matching anybody's intensity, we set the tone for how we play," Franklin said. "Minnesota's just the first test. It's going to be good to put that on tape and let the league know what the Green Bay Packers defense is all about."

Safety Evan Williams put the fourth quarter on the details.

"Just having the mental fortitude late in the game when you're tired, when it's late in drives to find a way to get off the field and do exactly what you're supposed to do," Williams said. "I feel like we put ourselves in a good spot, but at the end of the day, I said it before, but can't leave it up to the refs to make those type of calls."

Green Bay plays at the New York Jets on Sunday at noon CT.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers: Christian Watson details what the team must fix after Week 1 Vikings loss
articles.summary: Christian Watson caught both of the touchdowns the Green Bay Packers scored on Sunday and did not want credit for either one. Watson took a Jordan Love throw...
articles.body:
Christian Watson caught both of the touchdowns the Green Bay Packers scored on Sunday and did not want credit for either one.

Watson took a Jordan Love throw 81 yards to the end zone with 7:54 left in the first quarter, then caught a two-yard score with 18 seconds left in the first half that sent Green Bay into the locker room up 19-10. The Packers led 22-10 in the third quarter and lost 39-22 at U.S. Bank Stadium.

"Didn't do enough for us to win the football game," Watson said. "Obviously it was super excited coming in from the first half, feeling like everything was going the right way, but it's hard to be proud of anything when it didn't amount to anything for the team. So it's a tough one."

Minnesota scored 22 points in the fourth quarter, three touchdowns inside a span of 2 minutes and 39 seconds. Watson said the room saw it coming and could not stop it.

"Yeah, the coach said it best," he said. "Momentum is a strong thing, and we didn't respond, so once they got that momentum, they just kept on going."

He also declined to hang the loss on Matt LaFleur's decision to take points off the board and go for it on fourth-and-1 in the fourth quarter.

"I don't think that one play was anything," Watson said. "I think there was a lot of plays that kind of escalated into the result of the game today. But I think in every situation, you've got to find a way to execute better. And once it comes down to execution and we didn't execute, we needed to."

Watson on finishing: 'The only answer is yes'

Finishing games was the offseason emphasis in Green Bay. Watson got the question everyone in the building knew was coming, and he did not dodge it.

"I think the only answer is yes after a result like today," Watson said. "I think it just comes down to execution. We've got to find a way to execute in those critical moments. We've got to find a way, all 11, to be on the same page on offense, defense, special teams, everything. It comes down to crucial moments in the game, and we've got to find a way to come out on top of those if we want to come out on top of the game."

On the penalties, of which Green Bay had 12 for 98 yards to Minnesota's three for 15, Watson went where Tucker Kraft and LaFleur went.

"It was huge," he said. "We can't put stuff like that in the ref's hands. We've got to find a way to be disciplined and play sound football."

One game into a season, Watson signed a long deal to be part of

Watson entered Sunday on a four-year extension worth a reported $92.5 million, one of several deals Green Bay handed out this offseason on a list that also includes Jayden Reed , Devonte Wyatt and, as of Saturday, Tucker Kraft .

He was asked how a team digests a loss like this with 17 games still in front of it.

"We've just got to be open to critiquing ourselves and being hard on ourselves," Watson said. "Because obviously it's only one game, but we've got to be able to learn from the mistakes, learn from the whole game, and find a way to come out on top. Otherwise, we don't want to turn the wrong direction. We want to find a way to get back to where we're at."

Love finished 21-of-42 for 387 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Green Bay outgained Minnesota 419-239 and ran for 66 yards on 21 carries.

The Packers return to action against the New York Jets on Sunday at noon CT.
